title: FIG. 04 · Strata assembly
summary: Your round-1 C pick, rebuilt so it reads at a glance. Four plain, flat slabs drop in and close up into one stack on the left. Each has its job drawn on its face and its name on a straight leader. B's ledger on the right opens in place and moves the single red face, and A's head sits on top. No logo shapes appear anywhere.

reference.site: Round 1 · C (Stepped assembly) + A (head, plate) + B (ledger)
reference.borrowed: From C (and its Atlas reference), the composition: one engineering drawing of a single assembly on the left, exploded along one axis and documented with leaders, a dimension and a title block, with the detail held in a column on the right and a selection that travels down the layers. From A, the head grammar and the FIG. plate. From B, the four-row ledger that opens in place to 'What it is / In practice'.
reference.kelwin: C's nested L-plates are replaced by the STRATA primitive (DIRECTION-AC P2): four rectangular slabs (176 × 112 units, 12px thick) in true 30° isometric with occluding fills. They are drawn on the graphite inside a four-mark registration frame rather than on a plate, which keeps C's drawing-sheet feel and sets the section apart from the plated reframe and architecture figures on either side. Each top face carries one inscription naming its job: text rules for Narrative, a lit record grid for Data, a routing trace for Orchestration, and one open ring with a point riding it for Intelligence. Callouts are Mona 14px, coded 01–04 to match the ledger. One vertical dimension re-measures the stack ('4 layers' → '1 system'). C's red plane becomes the selected slab's red top face, with its inscription in paper and an 8px lift. C's uppercase title, tab cells, spec cells, big layer word, CTA cell, sheet frame verticals and crosshairs are gone. A's two-line head and its 'Built to compound' note sit on top. B's ledger (cols 9–12) is the section's one control and ends on a single quiet door.

addressed: A, B and C blended. From A: the head (red-square label, two-line statement, red rule, short lede, 'Built to compound' note) and its restraint. From C: the drawing on the left and the detail on the right, drawn like an engineering sheet with four corner registration marks and a small title block. From B: the calm ledger on the right.

The layered art on the left still animates the way you liked. The four layers drop in one by one, spread apart. Then they visibly close up into one stack while the measurement beside them changes from '4 layers' to '1 system'. After that the red layer steps down 01 → 02 → 03, just like C's red plane did.

Much easier to read. Every layer shows its job on its own face: lines of text = Narrative, a grid of records with the good ones lit = Data, one signal routed three ways = Orchestration, and a loop with a point riding it = Intelligence. Every layer is also named in plain 14px type with the same number, 01–04, as its row in the list on the right. The red layer is always the row that is open, so the drawing and the list read as one thing.

No logo symbol, and nothing that looks like it. The layers are plain rectangles: no L-shapes, steps, nested corners or core square. The layers are spaced so the red layer always shows as a whole rectangle and never as a corner-shaped sliver. The Intelligence layer was a target (rings with a centre dot) and is now one open loop.
Same kind of animation, new shapes: the red top face moving from layer to layer with a small lift replaces C's red plane sliding through the nested plates.

The list on the right reads cleanly. Each row has a number, a name, a one-line job and a +, and one row is open at a time to show 'What it is' and 'In practice'. C's tab cells, spec cells, big uppercase word and CTA cell are gone.

The section now ends somewhere. A single quiet link under the list, 'Find your weakest layer →', leads to the System Audit without adding a second red element. The title block, the frame's bottom marks and that link sit on one shared baseline.
motion: entrance (kit choreography): the label fades in; 'We don't deliver work.' and then the light 'We install systems.' rise out of their masks; the 48×2 red rule draws; the lede and note fade up. The four registration marks fade in at 300ms, and the ledger rows cascade up from 900ms, 80ms apart. The quiet door follows at 1.3s.

orchestrated moment (STRATA · planes stack): from 700ms the four slabs drop in one at a time in reading order 01 → 04 (−24px → 0 plus fade, 700ms, 140ms apart) at exploded spacing (pitch 148), with slab 01 already red. Each face's inscription plots as its slab lands: the text rules draw line by line, the records fade in column by column, the trace draws from its input outward with each node appearing as the line reaches it, and the ring sweeps round to its gap. The 01–04 callouts fade in beside their slabs. The dimension draws at 1.5s and reads '4 LAYERS'. At 2.0s the stack closes up to its installed pitch (148 → 112, so the outer slabs travel 54px; 700ms --ease-inout), with slabs, callouts, extension lines and dimension moving together. As the slabs land, the dimension value crossfades to '1 SYSTEM', the title block's state cell changes from EXPLODED to INSTALLED, and the dashed assembly lines register at the left and right corners.

stepped selection: at 3.0s and 4.2s the selection steps 01 → 02 → 03. The red top face crossfades to the next slab (400ms), that slab lifts 8px, its inscription turns paper, its callout brightens, and the matching ledger row opens in place while the previous one closes (360ms). The mockup rests on 03 · Orchestration about 4.6s in.
ambient: none; nothing loops after the sequence.

interaction: every ledger row is a button. A click opens that row, moves the red face and lift to its slab, and stops the automatic stepping. Kit behaviour applies: the row title nudges 6px on hover, the open row's + turns to −, and the door's arrow nudges 3px.

on the live site: the figure plays once when 40% visible (IntersectionObserver, no pin). The selection auto-steps every 1.4s while in view and stops for good on the first click. Reduced motion renders the final markup synchronously (installed, 03 selected, row 03 open) and starts no timers.
notes: The stage is 1336px tall, with 128px kit padding, an 88px two-line statement, and the figure 64px below the head (a 600px field plus a 56px caption row inside a registration frame, so 4 marks and no plate). The frame's top marks sit on the ledger's top rule, and its bottom marks, the title block and the door share one baseline. The statement is A's round-1 edit, 'We don't deliver work. / We install systems.'; 'Kelwin' moves into the lede, which no longer repeats 'compound' because the note carries it. Four layers: the source (RevenueOS.tsx) has three, and the Data copy comes from capability-data.tsx, as in round 1. Deliberate deviation from STRATA's 40–72px exploded spacing: the installed gap is 100px and the exploded gap 136px. Any tighter, and the slab above bites into each face, which hides the inscriptions and cuts the red face into an isometric chevron, the mark-like shape §4 bans. Geometry is generated in face coordinates (rev-stack/gen.py in the scratchpad), so every inscription stays in the visible part of its face even while its slab is lifted. C quotas: 1 drawing, 4 callouts (≤4 words each), 1 dimension line, 4 registration marks, and 1 title block of 3 cells, giving 10 annotation words. Every mono line is ≤ 16 characters. The section's red is the selected top face only. The door is the kit's quiet .ac-link, not a button, per DIRECTION-AC §5.2/§6.3. Copy to vet: the door label 'Find your weakest layer' (→ /audit).
